title: CausalHypothesis
description: An asserted causal mechanism between two measured phenomena, recorded with explicit confidence and uncertainty and DISTINCT from the observed dea:Correlation (CR-MET-012 section 6, Q22c). A hypothesis is a claim requiring validation; a correlation is an observation. The two MUST NOT be collapsed: a strong correlation is not evidence of causation, and asserting a mechanism from co-variation alone is a governance failure. validation_state records whether the hypothesis has been tested, not merely asserted.

cause_ref.description: The asserted cause. The direction is what distinguishes a hypothesis from a correlation.

effect_ref.description: The asserted effect of the cause.

mechanism.description: The asserted causal pathway. A hypothesis without a stated mechanism is an assertion, not a hypothesis.

confidence.description: Declared confidence in the asserted mechanism, distinct from the strength of any supporting correlation.

uncertainty.description: Explicit uncertainty: unmeasured mediators, plausible alternative mechanisms, and known limits of the inference.

validation_state.description: How far the hypothesis has been tested. asserted means nobody has tested it; correlation_supported means a co-variation was observed, which is weaker than validated; validated requires an experimental or quasi-experimental basis; refuted means the mechanism was tested and did not hold.

supporting_correlation_refs.description: The dea:Correlation records that were observed in support. Supporting correlations are evidence, not proof.

counter_evidence.description: Evidence AGAINST the hypothesis. A hypothesis with no recorded counter-evidence is either trivially true or not honestly recorded.

falsification_test.description: The test that would refute the hypothesis. A hypothesis with no falsification test is not testable.

responsible_party_ref.description: The accountable party for the hypothesis assertion.
